rationale: The objective is the max across ranks of per-rank summed NCCL kernel durations (median of 3 separately profiled runs; kernel time includes device waiting), with step_ms <= 1.05x baseline. Measured facts on this revision: one accumulated step issues exactly 13 SUM allreduces per rank on process group 0 / stream 17 - 12x 28,351,488 B plus 1x 157,541,376 B, totaling the full 497,759,232 B fp32 gradient payload - and every one of the 13 device kernels is ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL (grid 2x544, 2 channels) in both the discovery-hook execution_timeline (rank 0 sum 47.7 ms, rank 1 35.7 ms) and the separate nsys run (rank 0 sum 35.13 ms, 13 kernels). The warmed-worker nccl_tuning collector on the same leased GPUs logs Algo RING proto SIMPLE for exactly these sizes/dtypes (28,351,488 B x24, 157,541,376 B x2), i.e. NCCL's own tuner selects the bandwidth-efficient protocol for these payloads while the in-step collectives run LL, an actionable mismatch on this PCIe-only pair (NVML reports no NVLink; nvlink state not supported). Clean collective_calibration at the exact observed sizes gives ~1.995 ms per 27 MiB bucket and ~10.65 ms for the 150 MiB bucket, matching the late-arriving rank's in-step kernel durations, so the step already sits at the LL floor (~34.5 ms/rank); the remaining gap to the 38.09 ms objective baseline is inter-rank arrival skew paid as in-kernel waiting (original discovery: rank 1 entered the first bucket ~66.1 ms before rank 0 and summed 228.3 ms vs rank 0's 33.2 ms; baseline diagnostic samples 35.9/38.1/38.4 vs 42.7/34.7/35.2). The two selected groups share one dispatch target (c10d.allreduce_.default) and jointly cover all 13 collectives (call d0938de87369efd500322679 with 12 invocations, call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b with the 157,541,376 B bucket); replacing only one site would leave the 10.5 ms embedding bucket on the LL path and produce mixed reduction paths, so they are one coherent joint boundary. All calls in both groups are included in affected_calls. The DDP construction (bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view) lives in the frozen adapter, so the allreduce dispatch boundary is the one editable site through which every bucket collective flows.
hypothesis: Replacing both c10d::allreduce_ sites with an implementation that performs the identical SUM allreduce on a dedicated NCCL process group configured for bandwidth-bound large messages - created lazily and symmetrically on first use (collective-safe: both ranks hit the same bucket sequence), using the per-group knobs available in this worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129 (ProcessGroupNCCL.Options().config min_ctas/max_ctas/cta_policy and NCCL_PROTO applied before that group's communicator init) - will move the 13 collectives from RING_LL to SIMPLE-class bandwidth, roughly halving per-byte kernel time (~2.0 -> ~1.0-1.2 ms per 27 MiB bucket, ~10.6 -> ~5.5-6.5 ms for the 150 MiB bucket) and reducing the max-rank NCCL kernel sum from ~38 ms toward ~19-22 ms. SUM over the same world with identical inputs keeps every rank's reduced gradients bit-identical (atol=0/rtol=0 replica check and serial-reference checks unaffected); gradient bytes and step work are unchanged, so step_ms stays within 1.05x baseline aside from one-time lazy PG creation that warmup absorbs. Explicit unknowns, treated as hypotheses to test rather than facts: why the in-step communicator selects LL while the warmed worker selects SIMPLE (not established by any collector); the actual SIMPLE timing at these sizes (no timed SIMPLE sample exists, only the LL calibration); and the residual arrival-skew component, which protocol choice does not remove and which may keep the max-rank sum above the single-rank floor. If forcing the protocol on a fresh group proves ineffective, a fallback within the same boundary - coalescing the 13 bucket allreduces into fewer larger collectives on the same tuned group - still attacks per-op overhead and in-kernel wait, and stays inside the selected joint scope.
